title: Cascade tool executor with incremental result merge and recursion sentinel
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: Implement a cascade-style tool executor that incrementally merges tool outputs into the ongoing response stream while applying a lightweight recursion sentinel to detect and stop runaway loops. This ticket covers design, prototype, tests, and a staged rollout.
problem_statement: Current multi-tool execution paths either buffer all intermediate results until completion (increasing memory and latency) or inject results eagerly without proper provenance, which can cause inconsistent structured outputs and make recursion/looping difficult to detect. We need an approach that: 1) supports streaming responses to the client as tools complete, 2) merges tool outputs into an evolving structured document (with provenance annotations), 3) enforces recursion/loop protection without blocking legitimate multi-hop tool chains, and 4) remains compatible with existing function-calling and structured-output contracts used by the API and SDKs.
goals:
- Stream partial tool outputs to clients with deterministic merge semantics.
- Preserve provenance and source attribution for every injected result.
- Detect and throttle recursive tool invocation loops with low false positives.
- Provide compatibility layer so legacy SDKs can opt into incremental injection.
- Add metrics and observability for loop events, injection latency, and merge conflicts.
non_goals:
- Full rewrite of the orchestration layer or the serving runtime.
- Complex semantic reconciliation of conflicting tool outputs beyond structured merge heuristics.
- Addressing unrelated autoscaling or capacity provisioning issues (covered by Dedicated team tickets).
proposal_overview: Introduce a 'cascade executor' mode for the orchestration layer. Key ideas: 1) incremental result frames: tools emit framed results (structured JSON fragments, text segments, or embedding batches) that the executor can attach to an in-flight response stream; 2) merge policy: a pluggable merge policy that operates on the structured output contract (append-only arrays, field-level upserts with timestamps/priorities, and conflict buckets for manual reconciliation); 3) provenance envelope: every injected fragment carries metadata (tool_id, invocation_id, depth, parent_tool, confidence) so downstream consumers can reason about trust and fallbacks; 4) recursion sentinel: a lightweight counter and fingerprinting strategy that records repeated invocation patterns (tool chain signature + normalized prompt hash) and triggers configurable actions when thresholds are hit (warn, throttle, abort); 5) compatibility shim: a flag in the API and SDKs to opt into cascade mode; default remains legacy buffered mode to avoid regressions.
design_decisions:
- Use append-only framing for streaming text to simplify client consumption and replay semantics.
- For structured outputs, use field-level merge with conflict buckets rather than heuristic overwrites; this keeps deterministic behavior and surfaces conflicts for audits.
- Implement provenance as flattened metadata (string map) to avoid nested structures in logs and metrics.
- Recursion sentinel combines shallow depth counters (per-request) and a sliding-window fingerprint cache (LRU with TTL) keyed by tool-chain signatures to catch both immediate recursions and slower looping patterns.
- Rate-based throttling for tools implicated in loops rather than immediate hard kills to reduce false-positive user impact.
- Default thresholds: depth_limit=8, repeat_window=60s, repeat_count=3 (configurable via per-customer policy).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests for framing, merge policies, and provenance tagging.
- Integration test: a 3-tool chain that streams partial outputs; final merged structured output matches expected authoritative record and conflict buckets are populated when appropriate.
- Recursion tests: synthetic loop sequences trigger sentinel at configured thresholds and executor applies throttle/abort per policy.
- Backwards compatibility: requests without cascade_mode flag behave exactly as today (buffered injection).
- Metrics: new telemetry (injection_latency_ms, merge_conflicts_count, sentinel_triggers) emitted to console dashboards.
- Rollout: feature gated behind runtime-1.21 and opt-in API param. Optionally enabled for internal beta customers before wide release.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (prototype, 1 week): implement framing protocol in orchestrator, simple append-only text streaming, and basic provenance envelope. Add unit tests.
Phase 2 (merge policies + structured frames, 2 weeks): implement field-level merge, conflict buckets, and structured frame deserializers. Add integration tests.
Phase 3 (recursion sentinel + policies, 1 week): add sentinel cache, thresholding, and throttle strategies. Add load tests to ensure low perf overhead.
Phase 4 (compat shim + SDK changes, 1 week): add API flag, update SDKs to expose cascade_mode option, and add migration docs.
Phase 5 (beta rollout + monitoring, 1 week): enable for internal accounts, monitor sentinel triggers and merge conflicts, collect feedback and iterate.
Note: plan assumes close collaboration with SDK and Console teams to implement telemetry and rollout controls.
testing_and_validation:
- Unit tests: frame encoder/decoder, merge unit, provenance sanitizer.
- Integration tests: end-to-end simulated tool chain with mixed text/structured frames and induced conflicts.
- Load tests: run cascade executor at representative QPS to measure latency and memory compared to buffered baseline.
- Fuzz tests: randomized tool outputs to validate conflict bucket creation and safe client streams.
- Observability: ensure traces include invocation_id, depth, and merge decisions for post-mortems.
rollout_and_migration:
- Initially gate feature behind runtime-1.21.
- SDKs expose 'cascade_mode' boolean; default false.
- Internal beta: enable for 5 internal orgs and monitor for 72 hours.
- Gradual customer opt-in: ramp to selected third-party customers who signed up for early access.
- Full release: flip default after 90 days if metrics indicate stable behavior and acceptable conflict rates.
- Migration docs: include recommended merge policies for typical patterns (QA annotation pipelines, tool-augmented retrieval, multi-tool synthesis).
observability: Emit metrics: injection_latency_ms (p95/p99), merged_frame_count, merge_conflicts_count, sentinel_triggers_total, sentinel_actions_{warn,throttle,abort}. Add trace tags: cascade_mode=true, invocation_id, tool_chain_signature, depth. Add dashboard panels and alert: sentinel_triggers_total > 0.5% of requests over 5m should page on-call for investigation (configurable).
security_and_privacy: Provenance metadata may include tool identifiers—ensure we strip secrets and PII from envelope. Update audit log sanitizer to remove user content when required by customer policy. No key material or plaintext KMS tokens should be part of injected frames. Security review not required for initial prototype but will be re-evaluated for enterprise customers with stricter data retention requirements.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: false-positive recursion detection throttles legitimate long chains. Mitigation: conservative defaults, soft throttles (warnings), and per-customer overrides.
- Risk: merge conflicts produce confusing client-visible artifacts. Mitigation: conflict buckets surfaced via structured diagnostics and clear SDK helpers to collapse/resolve conflicts.
- Risk: increased CPU/memory overhead for merge logic. Mitigation: microbenchmarks and offloading heavy merges to background worker if needed.
- Risk: streaming partial outputs exposes intermediate PII. Mitigation: ensure customers opt-in and document data residency implications.
open_questions:
- Should the provenance envelope include a normalized confidence score for each tool? (pro: enables smarter merge policy; con: requires tool compliance).
- How aggressive should the sentinel fingerprinting be for variable prompts that normalize poorly?
- Do we need a policy-based rollback when many conflicts rapidly appear (indicating systemic tool regressions)?
